correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the real 2d-mode Fourier subspace, normalized Haar kernel K=2 sum cos, and minimal projection by translation averaging/unique multipliers. q3: K=3 Bin(d,1/3)-d and adjacent binomial mass identity gives 4d/3 P(Bin(d-1,1/3)=floor(d/3)); q4: each X has law of two fair signs, giving (2d/4^d) binom(2d,d). Independent full exact rational kernel enumeration for q=3,4 and d=1..8 matched all 16 formula instances. Symbolically checked fixed-residue shifted Stirling coefficient c_r=-(6r^2-18r+7)/24 and quaternary -1/8; high precision at d=120..6002 supports asymptotic. For the torus, symmetric characteristic function J0(2t), absolute-value integral, and log J0(sqrt(2/d)*s)=-s^2/(2d)-s^4/(16d^2)+O(s^6/d^3) give +1/(16d), justified by Gaussian-domination and |J0|<1 tail splitting. Independent Bessel quadrature at d=6,30,120 approaches 1/16, diagnostic only. The differences 2(c_r-1/16) yield -17/24, +7/24 and quaternary 2(-1/8-1/16)=-3/8, exactly the claimed signed limits. The O(d^-2) remainders follow fixed-residue Stirling and Gaussian-integral tail estimates; finite experiments do not substitute for the analytic d→∞ proof.
residual_risks: Numerical Bessel integrations are not certified interval bounds; analytic uniform tail splitting bears the asymptotic proof.
The torus extremizing sign is approximated in C(T^d), rather than attained as a continuous input; operator norm is the integral supremum.
Signs are established only for sufficiently large dimensions in each residue class, not for all small d.

value.rationale: The ambient axial first-frequency projection is a natural, canonical harmonic-reconstruction operator, with optimal uniform amplification measured by its projection constant. Its leading 2sqrt(d/pi) is alphabet-independent; the first nonzero discretization correction is a mathematically motivated higher-accuracy invariant which distinguishes the continuum, ternary grid and quaternary grid and reverses sign for one third of ternary dimensions. The signed q3-versus-continuum defect is an exact, reusable quantitative benchmark at the first scale on which the different alphabets separate. While the exact binomial identities and individual Stirling terms are textbook-level, the carefully quantified joined lattice/continuum correction, including a Bessel torus second term, supplies more than an arbitrary isolated numeric constant; no downstream paper-sized theorem is asserted.
residual_risks: The derivation is relatively short once known norm formulas are recognized, so its mathematical contribution is the motivated combined signed correction rather than a new projection theory.
Only q=3,4 axial and full torus are compared; no q≥5 or mixed-alphabet universal law is established.

final_claim: For d>=1, sharp real axial first-frequency Fourier projection norms on (Z/3)^d,(Z/4)^d and T^d have the submitted exact binomial/Bessel forms. Relative 1/d corrections are c0=-7/24,c1=c2=5/24 for q3, -1/8 for q4 and +1/16 for T^d, so the sqrt(pi*d)-scaled q3-versus-torus differences tend to -17/24 or +7/24 depending d mod3, and q4-versus-torus tends to -3/8.
limitations: Best-of-knowledge novelty; general Fourier/Hamming/Boolean prior results already determine component exact norms, so the joint signed correction alone is credited.
Asymptotic signed comparison not claimed for every small dimension; no explicit threshold.
Finite diagnostic checks and noncertified quadrature are not an infinite proof or formal verification.
